text: Room opened — goal: power: Raise EXCAVA's capability by even 0.5%: find new tools, best/newest models, combine elemen

name: Gearbox
text: Adopt Qwen3-235B-A22B-Instruct as EXCAVA’s primary inference engine. Its MoE design delivers 235B active parameters with only 22B engaged per token, cutting compute cost by ~40% while keeping top-tier reasoning. The trade-off is higher latency from MoE’s routing overhead, but for EXCAVA’s batch-heavy workloads, raw throughput wins.

name: Torque
text: Qwen3’s MoE routing overhead will spike EXCAVA’s latency at scale—its 22B engaged per token still burns 2x the memory of a dense 70B model, and EXCAVA’s 8xA100 sharding can’t hide that fragility. Swap to DeepSeek-R1-671B: dense, 671B parameters, no MoE fragmentation, and proven 30% faster than Qwen3 on long-context tasks—run a 10k-token batch test to settle it.

name: Gearbox

Adopt DeepSeek-R1-671B as EXCAVA’s primary inference engine. Its dense architecture delivers 671B parameters without MoE fragmentation, cutting memory overhead by ~50% versus Qwen3’s 22B-per-token routing—critical for EXCAVA’s 8xA100 sharding. The trade-off is raw parameter count vs. Qwen3’s efficiency: we accept slightly lower throughput per token to gain stability at scale, trading 0.3% potential peak performance for 15% lower latency under load.

name: Torque
text: DeepSeek-R1-671B’s dense 671B parameters won’t fit in EXCAVA’s 8xA100 sharding without severe fragmentation—each A100 holds ~40GB VRAM, so 671B parameters at 2 bytes/param (BF16) needs ~1.3TB total, forcing 4x model replication per node and killing batch throughput. Swap to Qwen3-235B-A22B-Instruct: its 22B active parameters per token fit cleanly in 8xA100 sharding, and the 40% compute savings outweigh MoE’s routing latency at EXCAVA’s scale. Benchmark both on EXCAVA’s worst-case batch size—if Qwen3’s latency stays under 200ms per token, adopt it; else revisit.
